scene: one adult sits reading at a table and turns the head sharply towards a doorbell beside the open door, the book still open in the hands; three short curved lines come from the bell. Nobody else is in the room.
must: a head turned sharply towards a ringing bell.
avoid: a hand cupped behind the ear, leaning towards a radio (luisteren); a person speaking into a phone (bellen); a person opening the door to a visitor (openen); eyes on the book and the head still (lezen).
alt: Iemand aan tafel met een open boek draait het hoofd snel naar een rinkelende bel bij de deur.
example_nl: Ik hoor muziek in de kamer.
example_en: I hear music in the room.

scene: one adult stands at a plain table and lowers a full glass of water with one hand until its base touches the table top; the base is just meeting the wood and the fingers are still round the glass. The eyes are on the glass and the table is bare.
must: a glass still held in the hand while its base lands on the table.
avoid: a glass lying on its side on the table (leggen); a glass planted flat with both hands already off it (neerzetten); a glass lifted off the table (pakken); a bottle at the lips (drinken).
alt: Een volwassene brengt een glas omlaag naar de tafel; de bodem raakt de tafel en de vingers houden het glas nog vast.
example_nl: Ik zet de fles op tafel.
example_en: I put the bottle on the table.

scene: one adult stands on a bare platform with the face turned towards the right edge, arms hanging, a small bag in one hand. A large round clock hangs high on the wall. There is no train, no track in view and nobody else in the picture.
must: one person standing still, facing forward, under a large round clock.
avoid: one adult mid-stride walking left to right (lopen); a hand held up flat towards a car with its brake lights on (stoppen); a person running with speed lines (rennen); a seated queue of people; a calendar.
alt: Iemand staat stil op een leeg perron met een tas, onder een grote ronde klok.
example_nl: Wij wachten op de bus.
example_en: We are waiting for the bus.

scene: one adult walks back into a kitchen through an open doorway carrying a bottle of milk in one hand, the other hand reaching to set it on the table where a second adult sits waiting with an empty glass.
must: a bottle carried back to a person who waits with an empty glass.
avoid: a mug lifted off a shelf (pakken); a bottle passed over a shop counter (kopen); a bottle tipped to the mouth (drinken); a bottle pressed to the chest while standing still (dragen).
alt: Iemand komt door een deur binnen met een fles melk voor iemand die met een leeg glas aan tafel wacht.
example_nl: Ik haal brood bij de bakker.
example_en: I get bread from the baker.

scene: two adults stand close together facing each other and each grips one half of the same long loaf of bread, both hands on it. The loaf is at the moment of breaking, one end tilted away and a few crumbs falling between them. Both look at the bread.
must: two pairs of hands breaking one loaf apart between them.
avoid: a slice held out in one hand towards another person (geven); coins and notes on a table between two people (betalen); an apple bag held out over a market stall (verkopen); one adult carrying a full box alone (dragen).
alt: Twee volwassenen houden samen een brood vast en breken het midden door; kruimels vallen.
example_nl: Wij delen een pizza.
example_en: We share a pizza.

scene: two adults stand facing each other half a metre apart, both with open mouths caught mid-word, one hand lifted and gesturing. Two short plain bars float above and beside each head, one bar per person. No other person is in the picture, and the bars carry no letters.
must: two people facing each other with an open mouth each and a plain bar above each head.
avoid: one adult alone facing the viewer with a speech bubble (spreken); one adult holding a phone hard against an ear (bellen); a raised finger and a silent second person (vertellen); a row of seated listeners (luisteren).
alt: Twee volwassenen staan tegenover elkaar, mond open, met boven elk hoofd een korte streep.
example_nl: Zij praten de hele avond.
example_en: They talk all evening.

scene: one adult walks from left to right along the bottom of the frame, and two metres behind them a second adult takes a stride in the same direction, head up, eyes on the walking gap between them. Plain ground, no path marks.
must: one adult walking behind another at a short distance, both heading the same way.
avoid: two people walking side by side, arms swinging together (samen lopen); a person leading the way and looking back at a second one (leiden); a person at a corner turning round (keren); an arrow or a dotted trail.
alt: Een volwassene loopt een paar stappen achter een ander in dezelfde richting.
example_nl: De hond volgt mij naar huis.
example_en: The dog follows me home.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with a closed jar pressed against the chest in one arm; the other hand grips the lid, the elbow lifted high, the face strained with the lips pressed together and the lid not yet turned.
must: a hand gripping a jar lid hard with a strained face.
avoid: a hand lifting a lid off an open jar (openen); a hand pouring from a jar (gieten); a person lifting a heavy box (heffen); a person pulling a rope (trekken); a pencil scribbling on paper.
alt: Iemand houdt een pot tegen de borst en grijpt met een gespannen gezicht het deksel vast.
example_nl: Ik probeer de pot te openen.
example_en: I try to open the jar.

scene: SKIP: posing a question is abstract and would reuse the speech bubbles of praten or the balance of a debate; the nearest literal sense, putting a box somewhere, is exactly the picture of zetten on this page.

one adult stands at a shop counter and lays a folded banknote flat on the counter towards a shopkeeper, who faces them with an open palm, the note halfway between the two hands. A price card stands in front of a box, and nobody holds any goods. Above the head of the CUSTOMER paying floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a banknote pushed flat across a counter into a shopkeeper's open palm.
avoid: a note and a paper bag of apples meeting on a counter (kopen); a note pressed into a lowered hand (geven); a bag of apples held out over a market stall (verkopen); a receipt torn from a till and a card.
alt: Iemand schuift een opgevouwen briefje over de toonbank naar de winkelier.
example_nl: Ik betaal de rekening in de winkel.
example_en: I pay the bill in the shop.

scene: one adult sits on a chair and leans forward with an open mouth, both hands shaping the air in front of the chest; opposite them a second adult sits still, eyes wide and fixed on the first. One broad speech bubble full of short plain lines arcs from speaker to listener.
must: one speaker leaning towards a seated listener beneath a long speech bubble.
avoid: two adults facing each other with one narrow bar above each head (praten); one adult alone facing the viewer with a small bubble (spreken); a book held open with both hands (lezen); a phone against the ear (bellen); letters inside the bubble.
alt: Een volwassene gebaart met open mond naar iemand die stil op een stoel zit.
example_nl: Mijn vader vertelt een grappig verhaal.
example_en: My father tells a funny story.

scene: one adult walks at the front of a small group with one arm raised straight forward and the hand pointing ahead; a second adult follows a step behind, and between them a thin taut rope is held at waist height by both. Both look ahead, not at each other.
must: one adult at the front with a raised arm, the second following on a rope.
avoid: one adult walking behind another, both arms swinging (volgen); a hand held out flat at a car with its brake lights on (stoppen); a person swinging a flat bat with both hands (slaan); a person pushing ahead through a line (dringen).
alt: Een volwassene loopt voorop met de arm vooruit; een tweede volgt aan een touw tussen hen.
example_nl: De gids leidt de groep rond.
example_en: The guide leads the group around.

scene: one adult shopkeeper stands behind a counter and turns a price sign round on its stand so it faces the viewer, both hands on it and eyes on the sign; a round loaf lies on the counter below the sign. The sign shows a coin shape and no digits.
must: a shopkeeper turning a price sign towards the customer, one coin shape on it.
avoid: coins and a note pushed across the counter (betalen); a paper bag of apples and a banknote meeting on the counter (kopen); a coin held out flat on an open palm (bieden); a hand pressing coins into the shopkeeper's palm (geven).
alt: Een winkelier draait met twee handen een bordje met een munt erop naar de kijker.
example_nl: Wat kost deze jas?
example_en: How much does this jacket cost?

scene: one adult stands at the front door of a small house and turns a key in the lock with one hand, a bag of shopping in the other, the door just opening inwards; the house is one plain outline with a window, and nobody else is in the picture.
must: a key turning in a front door held by a person with shopping.
avoid: a person with a suitcase walking away from a door (verlaten); a floor plan with a roof (bouwen); a bed with a person asleep in it (slapen); a person at a door with flowers for someone inside (bezoeken); a removal van (verhuizen).
alt: Iemand met een boodschappentas draait een sleutel om in de voordeur van een klein huis.
example_nl: Ik woon in een klein huis.
example_en: I live in a small house.

scene: one adult stands inside a changing booth with the curtain pulled back, one sweater half pulled off over the head with a plain shirt showing underneath, while the other hand holds up a different outfit on a hanger; a discarded hat lies on the bench.
must: a sweater half pulled off while a different outfit is held up on a hanger.
avoid: an adult putting on a jacket at a door (aantrekken); two coat hangers on a rail (kiezen); a person buying a shirt at a till (kopen); a person looking in a mirror (kijken); a suitcase being packed (inpakken).
alt: Iemand trekt een trui half uit en houdt met de andere hand een nieuwe outfit omhoog.
example_nl: Ik wil mijn haar veranderen.
example_en: I want to change my hair.

scene: One adult at a table presses both hands around a lump of wet clay on a board, thumbs pushed into the middle so the lump becomes a rounded pot; a small tool lies beside the board.
must: Two hands pressing a lump of clay into a pot shape.
avoid: a hand pressing a lump flat (kneden); a tower of blocks (bouwen); a pencil drawing a pot (tekenen); a finished pot on a shelf (maken).
alt: Iemand drukt met twee handen een klomp klei tot een pot.
example_nl: De kinderen vormen van klei kleine dieren.
example_en: The children shape small animals out of clay.

scene: one adult stands at the kerb with one flat hand raised towards an approaching car, the palm up at shoulder height; the car has both brake lights on and its front bumper a metre away, the bonnet dipping. The person looks at the car, not at the viewer.
must: a raised flat palm and brake lights on a car just short of it.
avoid: an adult standing still under a clock (wachten); one adult walking behind another on a rope (volgen); two adults breaking a loaf between them (delen); a hand flat on a shut door (sluiten); a red traffic light.
alt: Iemand houdt op de stoeprand een vlakke hand op naar een auto met brandende remlichten.
example_nl: De bus stopt voor het huis.
example_en: The bus stops in front of the house.

scene: two adults stand a step apart facing each other, each with one hand lifted at shoulder height and a wide smile, as friends who spot each other; neither carries anything.
must: two adults smiling, each with a hand lifted toward the other in recognition.
avoid: two adults shaking hands for the first time (ontmoeten); two adults hugging (omhelzen); one adult pointing at another across a room (wijzen); one adult waving at a bus (zwaaien).
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar en heffen allebei lachend een hand op.
example_nl: Ik ken je zus al jaren.
example_en: I have known your sister for years.

scene: one adult holds a baby in the arms and bends over it with the mouth open as if speaking to it; a second adult stands close beside with a hand on the chest and listens.
must: an adult looking down at a baby in the arms with the mouth open in speech.
avoid: an adult holding the baby up high (tillen); a parent feeding a baby from a bottle (voeren); two adults talking face to face (praten); a person pointing at an object (wijzen).
alt: Iemand kijkt naar een baby in de armen en spreekt; een tweede persoon staat er dichtbij en luistert.
example_nl: Ze noemen hun dochter Emma.
example_en: They are naming their daughter Emma.

scene: one adult in a post office holds an envelope above the slot of a postbox, the flap down and the lower edge just touching the opening; the fingers still hold it and it has not gone in. A second letter lies on a counter behind them, and no other person is present.
must: an envelope held at the mouth of a postbox, not yet dropped.
avoid: a cardboard box carried with both hands towards a half-open door (brengen); a box passing between two hands (geven); a letter laid flat on a table and let go (leggen); a phone at the ear (bellen).
alt: Iemand houdt een envelop boven de gleuf van een brievenbus, nog niet losgelaten.
example_nl: Ik stuur een bericht naar mijn vriend.
example_en: I send a message to my friend.

scene: one woman stands in a garden with her arms stretched wide and her face tipped up; a child and a dog run ahead of her and a bird sits on a branch.
must: a woman with outstretched arms in a garden with a child, a dog and a bird.
avoid: a house on its own (wonen); a person lying still on a bed (slapen); a hand held to the mouth to feel breath (ademen); a plain stone on the ground (bestaan).
alt: Een vrouw staat met uitgestrekte armen en gezicht omhoog in een tuin; een kind en een hond rennen voor haar uit en een vogel zit op een tak.
example_nl: Mijn oma leeft nog en woont in Utrecht.
example_en: My grandmother is still alive and lives in Utrecht.

scene: one adult sits on the edge of a bed with both eyes closed and one open palm pressed flat on a thick woollen scarf lying across the lap; the fingers are spread and the thumb rubs the cloth. Nothing is written or numbered, and no second person is present.
must: an open palm pressed flat on cloth, with the eyes closed.
avoid: an open palm on one's own chest (zijn); a cupped hand behind an ear (horen); a hand flat against a closed door (slaan); a palm held out flat over a radiator.
alt: Iemand zit op een bed en strijkt met een vlakke hand over een dikke sjaal.
example_nl: Ik voel me vandaag moe.
example_en: I feel tired today.

scene: a bicycle lies on its side on a pavement with its front wheel still turning; the rider sits on the ground rubbing one knee while two onlookers stand close with their hands to their cheeks.
must: a fallen bicycle with a rider on the ground and onlookers close around.
avoid: a person lying down on purpose (liggen); a person tripping over a stone (struikelen); a crowd watching a street show (kijken); a person helping someone up (helpen).
alt: Een fietser zit op de grond naast een fiets met draaiend voorwiel, twee mensen staan er geschrokken bij.
example_nl: Het ongeluk is gisteren op de hoek gebeurd.
example_en: The accident happened yesterday on the corner.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table and lays a flat white cloth down so that it lies flat on the table top, one hand still smoothing the last corner; a second folded cloth lies flat beside the first. The cloth is on the surface, not in the air.
must: a cloth lying flat on the table while a hand smooths it down.
avoid: a glass lowered onto a table with the hand still round it (zetten); a folded cloth seen from above in a row (vouwen); a cloth lifted off the table (pakken); a cloth hung over the back of a chair (hangen).
alt: Iemand strijkt op een tafel een doek plat neer; ernaast ligt een tweede doek.
example_nl: Ik leg de krant op tafel.
example_en: I put the newspaper on the table.

scene: one adult sits facing a second adult who spreads both arms wide while talking; the listener leans slightly forward with raised eyebrows, a relaxed smile and a slow nod, both hands resting open on the knees.
must: a nodding listener with a trusting open face opposite a talker with arms spread wide.
avoid: two people with a bar each above the head (praten); a person with a finger at the chin and a tilted head (denken); a hand raised flat in an oath (zweren); a person with both hands cupped to one ear (luisteren); clasped hands.
alt: Iemand zit met opgetrokken wenkbrauwen en een glimlach te knikken naar een ander die de armen wijd spreidt.
example_nl: Ik geloof je, want je liegt nooit.
example_en: I believe you, because you never lie.

scene: one adult stands at a shelf and closes one hand around the handle of a mug, the mug lifted a hand's width clear of the shelf and the arm drawn back; the other hand hangs empty at the side. Only that one mug is lifted, and the shelf holds no other cup.
must: a mug lifted clear off a shelf in one closed hand.
avoid: a bottle carried back through a door to a waiting person (halen); a box carried in both arms across the room (dragen); a note pushed along a counter (betalen); both hands laid flat on a full crate (gebruiken).
alt: Iemand sluit een hand om een mok op een schap en trekt die naar zich toe.
example_nl: Ik pak mijn jas van de stoel.
example_en: I grab my coat from the chair.

scene: one hiker stands on the flat top of a mountain with both arms raised high, a small flag pole at the peak and a steep path winding up behind.
must: a hiker with both arms raised on a mountain peak.
avoid: a hiker halfway up a slope with a stick (klimmen); a hiker looking up at a peak from below (kijken); a hiker sitting on a rock (rusten); a walker on a flat path (lopen).
alt: Een wandelaar staat op de top van een berg met beide armen omhoog.
example_nl: Na vier uur bereiken we de top.
example_en: After four hours we reach the top.

scene: one adult in a hard hat kneels on the floor and lowers a new house brick with both hands so a tower of four bricks stands beside it; the older half of a brick wall with wet mortar and a trowel reaches in from the left edge. The new brick is halfway down.
must: a new brick being lowered onto a growing wall.
avoid: three planks nailed into a crate at a table (maken); a small tree pressed into a garden hole (plaatsen); a closed machine case with a screwdriver in it (repareren); a finished house standing whole with a path (wonen).
alt: Iemand zet met twee handen een nieuwe steen op een muur die half af is.
example_nl: Zij bouwen een nieuw huis.
example_en: They are building a new house.

scene: one adult bends over a small child and holds out a wide open umbrella over both of them, the handle gripped with one hand and the canopy tilted towards a slanting rain of plain bold strokes; the adult's free arm is curved around the child's shoulders.
must: an umbrella held over a child while an arm shields the shoulders.
avoid: a note and a bag of apples meeting over a counter (betalen); one adult wrapping a blanket round a seated child (zorgen); an umbrella carried folded in one hand at the side (dragen); a raincoat on a hook.
alt: Iemand houdt een open paraplu boven een kind, de arm om de schouders, in de regen.
example_nl: Een helm kan je hoofd beschermen.
example_en: A helmet can protect your head.

scene: One adult stands with one hand raised beside the face, the middle finger crossed over the index finger; the eyes are wide and look at a closed door. The crossed fingers are a conventional gesture, not a literal action, and the scene is the only convention used.
must: A raised hand with crossed fingers beside the face.
avoid: a person waiting with a hand on a clock (wachten); a thumb tucked inside a fist (duimen); a person with a finger on the chin (denken); a hand waving (zwaaien).
alt: Iemand houdt twee gekruiste vingers omhoog naast het gezicht en kijkt naar een gesloten deur.
example_nl: Ik hoop dat het morgen mooi weer is.
example_en: I hope the weather is nice tomorrow.

scene: one adult sits facing a small radio on a plain table, the body leaning in, one hand cupped behind an ear and the head tilted towards it. The radio gives off three bold curved lines. The person is alone and looks at nothing else in the room.
must: one adult leaning in with a hand behind the ear, facing a radio.
avoid: two adults facing each other with open mouths and a bar above each head (praten); a head turned sharply from a book towards a ringing bell (horen); a phone held against the ear (bellen); a book open in the lap (lezen); letters on the radio.
alt: Iemand zit voorover naar een radio en houdt een hand achter het oor.
example_nl: Wij luisteren naar de radio.
example_en: We listen to the radio.

scene: one adult stands facing the viewer with a telephone held hard against one ear by that hand, the elbow raised out to the side, the other hand pressed flat on the hip, the mouth open and the eyes narrowed. A curled cord runs down from the phone to a pocket.
must: one hand holding a phone clamped to the ear, the mouth open.
avoid: two adults facing each other with a bar above each head (praten); a seated person under a long speech bubble addressing a listener (vertellen); one adult alone facing the viewer with a small bubble (spreken); a hand behind an ear while sitting at a radio (luisteren).
alt: Iemand houdt een telefoon tegen een oor, elleboog opzij, en praat met open mond.
example_nl: Ik bel mijn moeder vanavond.
example_en: I call my mother this evening.

scene: one adult crouches beside a child at a plain table, one hand on the child's shoulder and the other thumb raised toward the child's drawing; the child holds up a sheet with a plain house outline and beams.
must: a raised thumb and a hand on the shoulder beside a child holding up a drawing.
avoid: an adult handing a gift to a child (geven); an adult clapping both hands (klappen); an adult speaking with a raised finger (waarschuwen); an adult lifting a child into the air (tillen).
alt: Een volwassene hurkt naast een kind, legt een hand op de schouder en steekt een duim op naar de tekening.
example_nl: De juf prijst de leerling voor het mooie werk.
example_en: The teacher praises the pupil for the nice work.

scene: one adult stands at the edge of a pond and throws small pieces of bread from one hand towards three ducks on the water, the arm just swung forward and the crumbs in the air; the ducks swim towards the bread with their bills open.
must: bread thrown from a hand towards ducks on the water.
avoid: a ball thrown for a dog (gooien); a person eating a sandwich on a bench (eten); a dog on a lead (uitlaten); a person walking at the front of a group (leiden).
alt: Iemand aan de rand van een vijver gooit stukjes brood naar drie eenden.
example_nl: Ik voer elke dag de kat.
example_en: I feed the cat every day.

scene: one adult stands on the bottom step of a short flight of stairs with one foot planted on the step and the other foot just lifting off the pavement; one hand rests on the rail, the body is upright and the eyes are on the top landing with a closed door.
must: one foot lifting off the pavement onto the bottom stair.
avoid: a raised hand touching the rail at the top of the stairs (bereiken); both feet on the floor and the body straight, no stairs (staan); a person crouching to tie a shoe; a treadmill belt with speed lines (rennen).
alt: Iemand zet een voet op de onderste tree van een trap, de andere komt van de stoep.
example_nl: Ik stap in de bus.
example_en: I get on the bus.

scene: one adult stands behind a shop counter with both hands spread round a small pile of folded banknotes in front of them, at the instant a wooden till drawer is pushed open by the hip; a stack of three flat parcels lies beside the notes, and no other adult is present.
must: both hands around a pile of notes above an open till drawer.
avoid: a note pushed across the counter into a palm (betalen); a price sign and a straw basket under the counter (kopen); one banknote on a flat open palm (bieden); a pay slip with digits on it.
alt: Iemand achter de toonbank houdt met twee handen een stapel briefjes vast.
example_nl: Zij verdient goed in haar nieuwe baan.
example_en: She earns well in her new job.

scene: one adult walks along a station platform from left to right with a suitcase in one hand and a folded ticket in the other, the suitcase held low and trailing a few centimetres behind the leg; a single railway track with sleepers runs beside the platform, and no train is visible.
must: an adult crossing a platform with a suitcase beside an empty rail track.
avoid: both hands on a steering wheel on a road (rijden); a pilot in an aeroplane between clouds (vliegen); an adult standing still under a clock on a platform (wachten); an adult climbing the bottom step with a suitcase (stappen).
alt: Iemand loopt met een koffer en een kaartje langs een perron, naast het spoor.
example_nl: Wij reizen met de trein naar Parijs.
example_en: We travel to Paris by train.

scene: one adult kneels at the edge of a swimming pool and reaches down with one arm to grip the wrist of a child in the water; the child's hand is held above the surface and both their faces turn towards each other, with a second hand holding the pool edge.
must: an adult holding a child's wrist above the water at the pool edge.
avoid: a note held out in one hand while the other lifts a bag (betalen); two adults breaking a loaf between them (delen); a blanket wrapped round a seated child (zorgen); a lifebuoy thrown through the air (gooien).
alt: Iemand aan de rand van een zwembad houdt een kind in het water bij de pols vast.
example_nl: De brandweer redt de kat.
example_en: The fire brigade rescues the cat.

scene: one adult stands in a room with both arms raised high and a wide open smile, holding a paper garland at waist height between the hands; a second adult beside them raises a glass, and a small cake with a single candle sits on a table. Plain paper garlands hang behind them.
must: a person with both arms up beside a cake and a raised glass.
avoid: one adult with both arms up holding a gold cup (winnen); one person at a table with a tablecloth laid flat (leggen); a person behind a counter pushing notes into a till (verdienen); a ribbon across a road with a crowd.
alt: Iemand steekt de armen hoog met een slinger; ernaast heft iemand een glas bij een taart.
example_nl: Wij vieren morgen mijn verjaardag.
example_en: We are celebrating my birthday tomorrow.

scene: one adult faces a second adult who has just spoken; the first has raised eyebrows and an open mouth, and one hand lifts toward the other in answer.
must: raised eyebrows and an open mouth with one hand lifting toward the other person.
avoid: two people talking calmly (praten); a person shouting (schreeuwen); a person nodding yes (knikken); a person flinching from a loud bang (schrikken).
alt: Iemand trekt de wenkbrauwen op en steekt een hand op naar een ander die net iets zei.
example_nl: Hoe reageerde je op het nieuws?
example_en: How did you react to the news?

scene: one adult sits at a plain table over a sheet with a wobbly line drawn across it; a pencil is held in one hand and has just drawn a second, perfectly straight line directly beside the wobbly one, the eyes on the pencil point.
must: a straight line drawn beside a wobbly line by a pencil.
avoid: a teacher marking errors on a pupil's sheet (corrigeren); a hand drawing a fresh picture on a clean sheet (tekenen); a hand wiping out a whole sheet (wissen); a hammer fixing a loose fence post (repareren); a graph with an arrow.
alt: Iemand trekt met een potlood een rechte lijn naast een kronkelige lijn op een vel.
example_nl: De leerling verbetert zijn schrift.
example_en: The pupil improves his handwriting.

scene: one pregnant woman sits in an armchair with both hands on her round belly, a small empty cot beside her chair, her face turned toward the front door.
must: both hands on a round belly beside an empty cot.
avoid: a woman waiting at a bus stop (wachten); a woman cradling a baby in her arms (dragen); a woman pressing hands together hopefully (hopen); a woman lying in a hospital bed (bevallen).
alt: Een zwangere vrouw zit met beide handen op haar buik naast een lege wieg en kijkt naar de deur.
example_nl: Zij verwachten in maart een baby.
example_en: They are expecting a baby in March.

scene: one adult lies asleep under a blanket with the eyes closed and the mouth relaxed; over the head floats a conventional cloud of thought bubbles with a small sun and a plain open umbrella inside. This is the conventional dream cloud; draw it as one symbol and put no letters or numbers in it.
must: a sleeping person with a cloud above the head holding a sun and an umbrella.
avoid: a thought bubble with a question mark above a seated figure (denken); a lightbulb in a bubble above a head (weten); a figure lying flat on the bed with eyes open (liggen); a lamp with a light beam (lezen); letters in the cloud.
alt: Iemand slaapt onder een deken; boven het hoofd hangt een wolk met zon en paraplu.
example_nl: Ik droom vaak over de zee.
example_en: I often dream about the sea.

scene: One adult stands on grass with the arms still extended, just after shooting an arrow from a bow. The arrow flies past the left edge of a round target on a stand at the right. The target is untouched, and the adult looks at it, shoulders dropping.
must: an arrow passing beside a round target that is untouched.
avoid: a person running after a bus that has left (missen); an arrow stuck in the centre of the target (raken); a ball kicked into a net (scoren); a person alone at a table looking at a photo (missen); a bow held but not fired.
alt: Een volwassene heeft net een pijl afgeschoten; hij vliegt langs de rand van een ronde schijf die niet geraakt is.
example_nl: Hij schiet en mist het doel op een meter.
example_en: He shoots and misses the target by a metre.

scene: A steel kettle stands on a hob with the flame lit beneath it. Large bubbles rise inside a clear glass pan beside it, and thick steam bursts from the spout of the kettle. There is no person in this picture, only the kettle and pan. No text, no numbers.
must: a kettle on a lit hob with steam bursting from the spout.
avoid: a person stirring a pot with a spoon (koken); a cup of tea being poured out (schenken); an ice cube melting in a glass (smelten); a person touching a hot pan and pulling back (branden); a water tap running.
alt: Op een fornuis staat een ketel met vlammen eronder; er komt veel stoom uit en niemand is in beeld.
example_nl: Het water kookt, je kunt de thee zetten.
example_en: The water is boiling, you can make the tea.

scene: One adult sits alone at a small table by a window, chin on one hand, looking sadly at a framed photograph of another person standing on the table. The chair opposite is empty and pulled out. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a person gazing at a photo beside an empty chair.
avoid: a person running after a bus that has left (missen); two people hugging (houden van); a person waving at a departing train (zwaaien); a person asleep at the table (slapen); a phone call in progress (bellen).
alt: Iemand zit alleen aan een tafel bij het raam en kijkt naar een foto; de stoel ertegenover is leeg.
example_nl: Ik mis mijn vriendin, ze woont ver weg.
example_en: I miss my girlfriend, she lives far away.

scene: Two students sit at neighbouring desks, each with one blank results sheet in front of them. The student on the left slumps with the head hanging and a hand pressed to the forehead. The student on the right raises both arms and smiles. A pen lies on each desk. No letters or numbers on the sheets.
must: one slumped student beside a student cheering with both arms up.
avoid: a student holding a sheet with a big green tick, arms raised (slagen); a person sinking to the knees on the floor (zakken); a student writing at an exam desk (schrijven); a teacher handing over a diploma (geven); a shrug.
alt: Twee studenten zitten naast elkaar met een blad; de een hangt terneergeslagen met het hoofd, de ander steekt blij beide armen omhoog.
example_nl: Hij is gezakt voor zijn rijexamen.
example_en: He failed his driving test.

scene: One adult stands in front of a wall panel and presses a single round button with the tip of one index finger, the button glowing. The arm is stretched out and the adult looks at the button. No lift doors, no second person, no text or numbers on the panel.
must: one finger pressing a glowing round button on a wall.
avoid: a printer pushing out a sheet of paper (drukken); a hand turning a round tap (draaien); a fist knocking on a door (kloppen); a finger pressing a doorbell on a front door (bellen); a hand pulling a lever.
alt: Een volwassene steekt een arm uit en duwt met één vinger op een rond, oplichtend knopje in een muur.
example_nl: Druk maar op de groene knop.
example_en: Just press the green button.
